children: Air New Zealand's balance sheet can cope with headwinds buffeting the travel sector, including from higher fuel costs, Forsyth Barr says. Air New Zealand's operating data suggest robust yield improvement through 1Q on constrained capacity, analyst Andy Bowley says. Higher revenue is blunting inflationary pressures. "Air New Zealand is likely to generate material losses through FY27, adding to the recent pressure on its book equity or net tangible assets," he says. It estimates NTA falls to NZ$0.39/share in FY 2027, before recovering from FY 2028 as profitability returns. "We don't foresee any liquidity issues in the meantime or a need to raise additional equity, but continue to expect the company to defer capex where possible in order to prudently manage the balance sheet," Forsyth Barr says. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
